info.name: Francurial
info.description: Browser-automation task API: submit a task, check status, watch/control it live, resume past a CAPTCHA, and (internal) worker callbacks. See the repo README for full documentation, including the live WebSocket message protocol (not directly testable from this v2.1 Postman collection — see the note in the 'Live View' folder) and webhook signature verification.

request.description: Liveness check. Returns {"status": "ok"} with no auth required. Use this first to confirm the gateway is up before anything else.

Submits a task and returns 202 immediately with a task_id and a signed live_url — it does not wait for the browser work to finish. The test script below auto-saves task_id into the collection variable so the other requests just work.

credentials are kept out of the model's context entirely (substituted server-side); proxy and model are optional per-request overrides — omit either to fall back to round-robin PROXY / MODEL from .env.

item.name: Create Task (with explicit proxy + model override)

request.description: Same endpoint, minimal task — useful as a fast smoke test that a proxy/model combination actually works before pointing a real task at it.

item.name: Create Task (credentials only in instruction text)

request.description: Shows the fallback path: no structured "credentials" field this time — the email/password are only inside the free-text instruction. The model can't use type_credential() here (nothing was stored server-side for it to reference), so it falls back to typing the literal value it can already see in the goal text. This is safe (no new exposure — that value was already going to the LLM either way) but it is NOT encrypted at rest the way a real "credentials" field is, and it does appear in the task's audit trail as plain instruction text. Prefer the structured "credentials" field (see "Create Task" above) whenever you can.

Swap in a real endpoint of your own, or a scratch one from https://webhook.site to inspect what arrives. On completed/failed, the gateway POSTs {task_id, status, result, error} to webhook_url with an X-Signature header — HMAC-SHA256 of the raw JSON body, hex-encoded, using WEBHOOK_HMAC_SECRET. See the README's "Webhook payloads" section for a verification code snippet. Delivery retries with backoff on failure; check the webhook_deliveries table if one goes missing.

A plain Postgres row read — cheap to poll, never touches the live browser. Check status and wait_reason: status="waiting_input" with wait_reason="captcha" or "human_takeover" means it's parked waiting for you to open live_url and either solve something or click Continue (or call the Continue Task request below).

item.name: Continue Task (resume after CAPTCHA solved / human release)

request.description: Only valid while the task is in status="waiting_input" — 409s otherwise. Resumes the agent loop, which re-perceives the current page fresh (not a cached plan) and keeps working toward the original goal. Equivalent to clicking Continue in the live view page.

item.name: Live View
item.description: The live view has two parts, and only one of them is a plain HTTP request Postman can issue.

request.description: Returns the actual browser-facing HTML page (take/release control, continue, live frame, console/network log). This is meant to be opened in an actual browser, not really "used" from Postman — but issuing the GET here confirms the route is up and the signed token you got back from Create Task is valid. Copy the full live_url from a Create Task response and paste it into a browser tab to actually watch/control the session; the ?token=... query param is a signed, expiring HMAC token generated per-task, not something you set yourself.

item.name: (info) Live WebSocket protocol — not representable in this collection
item.description:
WS /v1/live/{task_id}?token=... is what the viewer page's own JS connects to for the actual video/control stream. Postman's v2.1 collection schema (what this file uses) is HTTP-request-only, so a native WebSocket request can't be exported into this JSON in a portable way — adding one risks shipping a collection that fails to import correctly elsewhere.

To test the WS endpoint directly: open a WebSocket connection (browser DevTools console, wscat, or Postman's own WebSocket Request feature added manually in the app) to the exact live_url's WS equivalent (same path, without /view). Server -> client messages: {type:"frame", data:"<base64 jpeg>"}, {type:"control_state", hasController, viewers}, {type:"console", level, text}, {type:"network", url, status}, {type:"session_ended"}, {type:"error", message}. Client -> server: {type:"take_control"}, {type:"release_control"}, {type:"continue"}, {type:"input", input:{kind:"mouse"|"key"|"wheel", ...}}. Full field-level detail is in the README's "Live WebSocket protocol" section.

item.name: CAPTCHA / Human Handoff Walkthrough
item.description: Reproduces the platform's most distinctive behavior end to end: the agent tries a CAPTCHA itself, hands off to a human when it can't solve it, and resumes exactly where it left off. Run these in order.

item.name: 1. Create Task Against a Protected Site

request.description: chatgpt.com sits behind a Cloudflare Turnstile check for automated traffic, which reliably triggers the handoff path for this walkthrough. Any Cloudflare- or reCAPTCHA-protected URL works the same way.

Poll this a few seconds after step 1. Once the agent hits the challenge and can't solve it itself, status flips to "waiting_input" with wait_reason="captcha" and control_state="human" — that's your cue to open live_url.

item.name: 3. (manual) Open live_url, solve the challenge, click Continue
item.description: Copy the live_url from step 1's response into a real browser tab. You'll see the actual live session — solve the CAPTCHA there, then click the Continue button in the page (or just run step 4 below, which does the same thing via the API).

request.description: Resumes the agent right where it left off — it re-perceives the now-cleared page fresh rather than replaying a cached plan. Poll Get Task Status again afterward to watch it keep going.

item.name: Internal (worker-only, for debugging)
item.description: Authenticated with X-Internal-Secret (INTERNAL_SHARED_SECRET), not the public X-API-Key. These exist for the worker to claim tasks, report status, and append audit entries — keep them off any public ingress in a real deployment.

request.description: Called by the worker right after popping a task off the Redis stream. Records which worker/pod owns the task (for live-view WS routing) and returns the decrypted url/instruction/credentials/proxy/model needed to actually execute it.
Partial update — only fields present in the body are changed. wait_reason must be sent as an explicit null (not omitted) to clear it once a task resumes.

Appends one row per agent-loop event (perceive/reason/act/captcha_*/human_*). Sensitive keys (password, email, credentials, proxy) are redacted server-side before storage regardless of what's sent here.
